A two-layer guarantee that a green npm run check cannot mean 'executed nothing': the test pattern is handed to node as an argv string and never reaches a shell, scripts/verify-test-coverage-floor.mjs pins the runner command and verifies check actually invokes it, and scripts/run-test-suite.mjs asserts the executed-test count the runner itself reported after the run

ownership.forbidden_paths_note: The globs **/*secret* and **/*credential* were removed: they forbade this package's own declared outputs (the secret scanner and its test), a contradiction the ownership validator could not see until it began comparing outputs against forbidden_paths. Replaced with the extensions that carry actual key material. A filename mentioning "secret" is not a secret; a private key file is.

The test-integrity guard is a TRIPWIRE, NOT A CONTROL, and has no self-anchor. A change that edits a guarded file and its digest in test-kits/integrity-manifest.json together passes. Independent review confirmed by construction that no in-repository control can close this: any verifier inside the mutable set can be replaced by an accept-always verifier. The anchor is human review of the diff under RFC-2026-002 and protected CI, which remains an open Gate G0 requirement blocked on an external constraint. Everything OUTSIDE that class -- an unprotected suite, phantom declarations, an escaping path -- is closed. UPDATED 2026-10-06 BY A0: the outside anchor this entry called missing now exists in part. main is protected (required status check bootstrap, strict, admins enforced; verified live and recorded in evidence/g0-tracker-th.md), and .github/workflows/ci.yml runs the guard as its own step. What is still missing is a required review: the human half of the anchor is the Product Owner reading the diff. The tripwire stays open as a limitation, not a defect to fix here.

Text as recorded: A trailing '&' in package.json's check script backgrounds the whole && chain, so `npm run check` returns 0 before any step's exit code matters. Independent testing demonstrated it, and the integrity digest does NOT help: the exit code is already 0 whether or not the manifest is updated. No control inside the scripts that check invokes can prevent this, because the exit code is decided by the shell operator in the script itself. The caller must invoke the guard as its own step: .github/workflows/ci.yml should run node scripts/verify-test-coverage-floor.mjs as a separate step rather than relying on npm run check alone. That file is owned by WP-0A-A0-001 and is read-only to this package, so the change is referred to the Integration Owner under the RFC path rather than made here. ci.yml is now digested so the omission is visible.
